item.title: [Itrfoundation] Nearly $1 Billion in Local Bonds on Iowa’s November Ballot
item.description:
Iowa voters will decide more than who represents them in public office this November. Across the state, local governments are asking voters to approve nearly $1 billion in borrowing, along with several tax and governance measures that could affect their communities for years to come.

According to Iowans for Tax Relief Foundation's review of the November 3,2026 ballots, there are 62 local public measures, including 44 general obligation and/or revenue bond questions, meaning that public debt accounts for the largest share of the ballot questions.  Together, local governments are seeking approximately $955 million in borrowing authority. item.title: [Pioneerinstitute] Massachusetts’ Declining Unemployment Rate is the Result of a Shrinking Labor Force
item.description:
At first glance, the latest unemployment numbers for Massachusetts look like good news. The state’s unemployment rate fell to 4.3 percent in August, its lowest level since March 2025 and down from a recent high of 4.8 percent in February, according to data released September 18 by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

But a falling unemployment rate doesn’t always signal a stronger labor market. A closer look shows that Massachusetts employers are still cutting jobs, and that unemployment is falling mainly because fewer residents are working or looking for work at all.

The post Massachusetts’ Declining Unemployment Rate is the Result of a Shrinking Labor Force appeared first on Pioneer Institute.
